requirements.quote: `proposeMemory` writes only `memory_proposal` rows (status `proposed`); no `memory_item` row exists until `confirmMemory` runs; a test asserts that no code path inserts a `memory_item` without a confirmed proposal or a lawyer-authored note. [type:unit]

Each memory item has layer (M1, M2, M3, M4, M6, M7), key, value, scope (user, workspace, matter), source anchor or `manual`, status (`active`, `paused`, `deleted`), confidence and confirmation state; layers outside that set are rejected. [type:unit]

Scope in SQL: a matter-scoped item is returned only for its own matter; reading it with another matter's id returns nothing at the query level (RLS plus predicate), proven by tests that attempt cross-matter reads. [type:api]
M4 court notes are private to the author by default; marking one chamber-shared requires owner role and is audited; non-owners cannot flip it. [type:api]
Clerk reads of M3, M4 and strategy-typed M1/M2 values return nothing via the column-scoped view and the policy function; an e2e API test covers each layer. [type:api]
M6 relationship memory accepts only a person linked as an existing client or professional contact; creating M6 for a non-client is rejected. [type:unit]

`proposeFromEdit` turns a repeated edit pattern (same edit made 3 times across 3 briefs or drafts) into a single rule proposal with evidence ('You added carry vakalat copy to the last 3 first hearings. Save?'); dismissed proposals are not re-proposed for 60 days. [type:unit]
`proposeFromCorrection` creates M7 alias proposals from user corrections to party or matter matching (for example 'Rajan' = 'M. Rajan s/o Murugan') and dedupes with existing aliases. [type:unit]

Edit, pause and delete work per item; delete removes the value immediately and queues embedding purge so embeddings are gone within 24 h, verified by a time-travel test; export includes active items. [type:unit]

`recordUsage` logs each time memory influences an output (brief, draft, matching) with the item id; `getMemory` for output includes citations so the UI can render 'because of your note on <date>'. [type:unit]

Memory values are envelope-encrypted with the workspace key (via #21 utilities when available, else the storage package's crypto helper) and never sent to a provider outside India-only mode; no memory content is used for training. [type:unit]
`tenureMetrics` returns correction rate and confirmation rate by tenure week and brief-accepted-unedited rate, aggregate within the workspace only. [type:unit]
No memory item or proposal can describe a judge or bench (denylist check on keys and a content guard); attempts are rejected with a clear error. [type:unit]
Per-member 'pause all memory' switch stops proposals and use immediately. [type:api]
Cross-tenant tests pass: a user in workspace A cannot read or mutate this feature's rows in workspace B via SQL, service, server action or API, including a user who belongs to both. [type:api]
Every new tenant table has `workspace_id uuid not null`, an RLS policy using `app.workspace_id`, and is covered by the CI cross-tenant suite. [type:unit]
Inputs are validated with zod schemas from `packages/validators`; no `any` appears in exported types. [type:unit]
